title: HeroDevs Open Source Sustainability Fund
description: HeroDevs' $20,000,000 fund for maintainers of open source developer tools under an OSI-approved license whose versions are near or past official end of life. Grants of $2,500 to $15,000 fund ongoing open source work and best practices in releases, communication, documentation, support and processes. Applications are open with no stated deadline.
reward: Grants from $2,500 to $15,000 per project (the application form says accepted applicants receive between $2,500 and $250,000 in donations)

rules: No deadline is stated; the fund page links straight to the application form.

Eligibility: you maintain an open source project under an OSI-approved license; its versions are near or past official end of life; the project is a developer tool; you are ready to keep users secure and CVE-free.
The fund page says grants range from $2,500 to $15,000. The application form description says accepted applicants receive between $2,500 and $250,000 in donations.

Applicants are assessed against best-practice criteria in five areas: releases and versioning, communication and transparency, documentation, support and deprecation handling, processes and support tiers.
After you apply, a team member confirms receipt and reviews the application; if approved, HeroDevs contacts you to begin criteria review and implementation. No timeline is stated.
Accepted projects receive a Best Practices Form, a self-service tool for documenting existing practices and getting guidance on improvements, and are expected to align with the program criteria.
Only the email field is marked required on the form; the other questions are optional.
